summary: The FRBPA (Full) 95% credible upper limit on g_agamma from Fig. 3 is correctly identified as a genuinely new measured bound (first FRB polarization array), with units, confidence, and representative tabulated points matching the paper's abstract and figure; the highlighted plot shades the correct one-sided upper-limit region with a legible label and no unrelated co-highlighting.

verdict.summary: The FRBPA (Full) 95% credible upper limit on g_agamma from Fig. 3 is correctly identified as a genuinely new measured bound (first FRB polarization array), with units, confidence, and representative tabulated points matching the paper's abstract and figure; the highlighted plot shades the correct one-sided upper-limit region with a legible label and no unrelated co-highlighting.

result_identity.evidence: AxionPhoton, g_agamma [GeV^-1] vs m_a [eV]. Headline is the thick red 'FRBPA (Full)' 95% upper-limit curve in the upper panel of Fig. 3 (p.13), the full-correlation joint analysis of three repeating FRBs. Matches paper subject (cosmic birefringence, Chern-Simons coupling).

novelty.evidence: New measured exclusion (not projection; is_projection=false). Paper (Sep 2026) presents 'constraints from an FRBPA for the first time' (p.2) and places new 95% credible upper limits (abstract). FRBPA is weaker than existing compilation limits in this range but is a genuinely new, distinct measured bound; extraction selected the combined FRBPA curve explicitly.

confidence_level.evidence: Abstract states '95% credible upper limits on the Chern-Simons coupling'; Fig. 3 caption (p.13) says '95% upper limits'. Extraction uses confidence_level=0.95, directly supported, not a placeholder.

conventions.evidence: Mass in eV, g in GeV^-1 consistent with paper. DM density: paper rho_0=0.4 GeV/cm^3 (Eq. 2.5, p.4); plotting method rescales to repo 0.45 via sqrt(0.4/0.45)=0.9428 (g ~ 1/sqrt(rho)), correct direction (higher density -> stronger/smaller limit). Data stored paper-native. Minor approximation noted in advisory finding.

numerical_agreement.evidence: Endpoints verified against abstract: 1e-23 eV -> 2.5469e-13 (10^-12.59) vs quoted 10^-12.6; 1e-18 eV -> 1.343e-8 (10^-7.87) vs quoted 10^-7.9. Non-monotonic bump at 5.6e-19 eV (2.1e-8) matches the BF peak feature described p.12-13. Overall staircase shape matches the red FRBPA (Full) curve in Fig. 3.

highlight_target.evidence: In both highlighted PNGs only the FRBPA red region is accented. It shades continuously UPWARD from the curve to the plot top (correct one-sided upper-limit direction). The fill terminates near ~2e-19 eV because the limit weakens above the plot's top (10^-9), physically correct; no invented endpoint stripes or second boundary. Left edge is the data start at 1e-23 eV.

visibility.evidence: Highlighted view shows the full relevant range (1e-23 to ~2e-19 eV on-screen) with legible 'FRBPA' label at lower-left. Curve boundary interpretable. In the full compilation view the limit is occluded by stronger existing limits (Planck/PSR J0437/PPTA), which is expected for a weaker new limit; highlighted view provides identification.

findings.description: The repo applies a uniform sqrt(0.4/0.45) density rescaling to the whole curve, but the paper's signal (Eq. 2.5, p.4) is a two-component model combining the Earth term (rho_0=0.4) and source gNFW host densities (~0.4-2.2 GeV/cm^3, marginalized). A single-density rescale is an approximation.
findings.evidence: Eq. 2.5 and Sec. 3.4 (p.10): source densities comparable to local; paper states the full two-component superposition must be used, not a source- or Earth-dominated form.
findings.requested_change: None required; the ~6% correction is within extraction precision and is documented in the data header. Consider noting the two-component approximation in the entry comment.
